title: Unreachable NaN guard in updateCell push branch
description: updateCell computes num = val === "" ? safeDefault : (Number.isNaN(parsed) ? safeDefault : parsed). safeDefault comes from resolveDefault(), which is guaranteed non-NaN (returns 1 on NaN). parsed is only used when it is not NaN. So num is always a finite number. The new-entry push then writes value: Number.isNaN(num) ? 0 : num, but Number.isNaN(num) can never be true, so the ': num' branch is the only reachable one and the '0' fallback is dead.
evidence: Line 67: const num = val === "" ? safeDefault : (Number.isNaN(parsed) ? safeDefault : parsed). Line 70: next.push({ [factor]: level, value: Number.isNaN(num) ? 0 : num }). num cannot be NaN -> fallback 0 unreachable; the map branch (line 68) correctly uses num directly without the guard, confirming intent.
behavior_preservation: value: num is identical because num is never NaN; matches the sibling map branch which already uses num unguarded.
